newsitem.title: USA: Restrictions delay Houston Ship Channel traffic.
newsitem.headline: Restrictions delay Houston Ship Channel traffic.

text.p: A barge accident which occurred on Thursday along the Houston Ship Channel has delayed 16 inbound and 20 outbound deep draft ships, the Houston Ship Channel Pilots said on Friday.

Barges, tows and ships with drafts of 12 feet or less are still able to sail past the site where six large tanks fell overboard on Thursday and sank, blocking a section of the channel, U.S. Coast Guard officials said.
The accident has delayed traffic and restricted shipping past light 52 and light 56, where a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers sonar ship is searching for the tanks.

Deep-draft tankers can still reach refineries near Galveston and Texas City, but there is no deep-draft traffic into the Port of Houston along the ship channel, the waterway linking Houston's refinery row with the Gulf of Mexico.

The tanks included two measuring 38-feet in length and 11- feet in diameter along with four smaller tanks loaded with zinc bromide. The tanks fell overboard after the barge was swept by the wake of a passing ship on Thursday.
